name: Monument to the Third International, 1919–1920
description: Model of a 400-metre double helix of iron and glass designed by Vladimir Tatlin in 1919–1920 as the headquarters of the Communist International in Petrograd. Only models were built.
failedFuture: A tower meant to be both headquarters and monument of a new international order. It was never built; only models were made.
source: Leleu, N. (2007). The Model of Vladimir Tatlin's Monument to the Third International. Tate Papers.
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Efecto presente verificado en Wikipedia con tres fuentes citadas (UEA 2017, The Guardian 2017, RBC 2021); pendiente abrir las dos últimas en el original.

presentEffect.text: Models are held at the Moderna Museet, the Tretyakov Gallery and the Centre Pompidou. A 1:42 model was built at the Royal Academy in 2011 and at the Sainsbury Centre in 2017, and has stood in its sculpture park since 2018. Ai Weiwei's Fountain of Light (2007) at the Louvre Abu Dhabi is modelled on the tower, and the SKA Arena in Saint Petersburg (2023) was designed with inspiration from it.
presentEffect.source: Wikipedia, "Monument to the Third International" (citing a UEA press release, 2017; Oliver Wainwright, The Guardian, 7 November 2017; RBC, 2021).

name: Plan Voisin de Paris, 1925
description: Le Corbusier's 1925 proposal to replace part of central Paris, including the Marais, with glass towers set in parkland. Shown as a diorama at the Esprit Nouveau pavilion.
failedFuture: A central Paris cleared and rebuilt around eighteen identical skyscrapers set in roads and parks: a city planned as a machine for modern life. It was never carried out.
source: Le Corbusier, Oeuvre complète, vol. 1 (extracto publicado por Archiweb sobre el Pavillon de l'Esprit Nouveau).
license: Derechos reservados (ADAGP/FLC): pedir autorización o buscar otra imagen
status: Efecto presente atribuido vía Wikipedia (Treuttel 2017; Monclús y Díez Medina 2018); los originales no se han consultado.

presentEffect.text: Wikipedia reports that La Défense 'drew inspiration from Plan Voisin', especially its concrete slab foundation (Treuttel, 2017), and that the plan had significant influence on Brasília (Monclús and Díez Medina, 2018).
presentEffect.source: Wikipedia, "Plan Voisin" (citing Jérôme Treuttel, 2017, 'From Open Plan to Public Space'; Monclús and Díez Medina, 2018).

name: Palace of the Soviets, Moscow, 1931
description: Plans for the Palace of the Soviets, a congress hall and administrative centre planned on the site of the Cathedral of Christ the Saviour, near the Kremlin.
failedFuture: A palace of congresses and administration for the Soviet state, planned on the site of the Cathedral of Christ the Saviour after the Central Executive Committee decided on 13 July 1931 to build it there. The palace was never built.
source: Architectuul, "Palace of the Soviets". Y Tsereteli reconstruction: Harvard, Russia's Postcommunist Past, History and Memory 21.1 (2009).
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Efecto presente verificado en Wikipedia: decisión de 13 de julio de 1931, piscina de 1958, catedral consagrada el 19 de agosto de 2000.

presentEffect.text: The foundation pit became the Moskva Pool in 1958. The Russian Orthodox Church received permission to restore the cathedral in February 1990, and the rebuilt Cathedral of Christ the Saviour was consecrated on 19 August 2000 on the same site.

name: Plan for Greater Baghdad, 1957–1958
description: Drawings of Frank Lloyd Wright's Plan for Greater Baghdad: a cultural centre, opera house and university planned for an island in the Tigris.
failedFuture: A cultural centre, a circular opera house and a university planned by Frank Lloyd Wright on an island in the Tigris at the invitation of King Faisal II. The plans were dropped after the king's assassination.
source: WNYC / NYC Municipal Archives, "Frank Lloyd Wright's Plan for Iraq" (2010). Allison, J. (2008), "Arabian Opera Nights", Opera 59/1.
license: Derechos reservados (Frank Lloyd Wright Foundation Archives): pedir autorización
status: Efecto presente verificado en Wikipedia (Gammage). La fuente no da la fecha del diseño de Bagdad; se usa 1957, año del encargo de Gammage.

presentEffect.text: Wright adapted the circular opera house for the Grady Gammage Memorial Auditorium at Arizona State University. It opened on 18 September 1964, completed by William Wesley Peters after Wright's death, and is still in use.

name: Ideal city of Chaux, 1773
description: Claude-Nicolas Ledoux's Royal Saltworks at Arc-et-Senans was authorised by an edict signed on 29 April 1773, and construction began in 1775.
failedFuture: An ideal city planned around the saltworks. It was never started: only the diameter and a semicircle of buildings were completed.
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Verificada con Wikipedia. Año de concepción de la ciudad ideal no confirmado; se usa 1773, el del edicto de la salina.

presentEffect.text: The complex has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1982.
presentEffect.source: Wikipedia, "Royal Saltworks of Arc-et-Senans" (citing the UNESCO World Heritage list, ID 203).

name: Plan of Chicago, 1909
description: Daniel Burnham and Edward H. Bennett published the Plan of Chicago in 1909.
failedFuture: A reshaped city of diagonal avenues, consolidated railroad terminals and a civic centre. The Grant Park cultural centre was blocked by a state supreme court ruling, the civic centre at Congress and Halsted was never seriously pursued, only the Ogden Avenue diagonal was built, and only Chicago Union Station (1925) of the planned terminal consolidation.
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Verificada con Wikipedia. Pendiente comprobar la cifra de la costa (29 millas) en la fuente original.

presentEffect.text: Of the city's 29 miles of lakefront, all but four miles are today public parkland. Wacker Drive was created, and Michigan Avenue was renovated, widened and extended.

name: Cité Industrielle
description: Tony Garnier's model city for about 35,000 inhabitants, with separate zones for industry, housing and leisure, developed between 1901 and 1904 and published in 1917.
failedFuture: A city planned as a single industrial organism, with separate zones for industry, housing and leisure, which Tony Garnier exhibited in 1904 and published in 1918. As a whole city it stayed on paper.
license: Tony Garnier (murió en 1948): dominio público en la UE desde 2019. Verificar la imagen.
status: Corregido: la Wikipedia da 1918 para la publicación (no 1917). La cifra de 35.000 habitantes se quitó del texto por no estar verificada. Efecto presente verificado en Wikipedia; falta confirmar qué sigue en pie del barrio y el estadio.

presentEffect.text: Garnier built parts of his vision in Lyon: the Grange-Blanche Hospital (1910–1927), now the Édouard-Herriot Hospital and still in use, the Quartier des États-Unis housing (1919–1935) and the Stade de Gerland (1914–1918).

name: Fordlândia, 1928
description: Henry Ford's company established Fordlândia in the Amazon rainforest in 1928 to secure cultivated rubber for its cars.
failedFuture: A model town to end Ford's dependence on European rubber. Henry Ford II sold it back to the Brazilian government in 1945 at a loss of over $20 million, and, as NPR reported in 2009, 'Not one drop of latex from Fordlândia ever made it into a Ford car.'
source: Wikipedia, "Fordlândia" (citing Ben Macintyre, The New York Times, 2009; NPR, 2009).
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Verificada con Wikipedia; pendiente abrir NPR 2009 y The Guardian 2016. La fuente no da una referencia para los detalles de los edificios.

presentEffect.text: About 3,000 people lived there in 2017 (The Guardian, Drew Reed, 2016), and it is now a district of Aveiro. Most original buildings remain: the 50-metre water tower still operates, and the workshop, sawmill and kiln still stand. The hospital was dismantled by looters.

name: Città Nuova
description: Antonio Sant'Elia's drawings for the Città Nuova, a futurist city of towers, elevated roads and multi-level stations, shown in 1914 in Milan.
failedFuture: A futurist city of towers, elevated roads and multi-level stations, sketched by Antonio Sant'Elia from 1912 to 1914. He was killed on 10 October 1916 aged 28 and most of his designs were never realised.
license: Dibujos de Sant'Elia (murió en 1916): dominio público. Verificar la imagen.
status: Efecto presente atribuido (Goldberger 1986; Irish Arts Review) vía Wikipedia; pendiente abrir los originales.

presentEffect.text: Paul Goldberger (The New York Times, 1986) cited Sant'Elia as a precursor to architects such as John Portman and Helmut Jahn, and the production design of Metropolis (1927) and Blade Runner (1982) is described as indebted to his ideas (Irish Arts Review).
presentEffect.source: Wikipedia, "Antonio Sant'Elia" (citing Paul Goldberger, The New York Times, 1986; Irish Arts Review, 'Green Energy').

name: Dymaxion House, 1928–1930
description: Buckminster Fuller's Dymaxion House was completed in 1930 after two years of development and redesigned in 1945, in the version known as the Wichita House.
failedFuture: A house meant to be mass-produced. It was not produced industrially because of tooling costs, and no Dymaxion house built to Fuller's intentions was ever lived in.
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Verificada con Wikipedia. Corregido: 1930 de finalización (no 1927–1929).

presentEffect.text: The restored round aluminium prototype was donated to the Henry Ford Museum in 1990 and installed indoors there in 2001 with a full exhibit.

name: Southwest Expressway, Boston
description: The Southwest Expressway was planned from 1948, in William F. Callahan's Master Highway Plan for Metropolitan Boston, to bring an eight-lane highway into the city along the former railroad right-of-way through Roslindale, Forest Hills and Jamaica Plain.
failedFuture: An urban motorway through Boston's neighbourhoods. In 1970 Governor Francis Sargent declared a moratorium on expressway construction inside Route 128, and the project was formally terminated in 1972 after public pressure.
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Verificada con Wikipedia. Corregido: la cancelación formal es de 1972 (moratoria de 1970).

presentEffect.text: The cleared right-of-way now carries two Orange Line tracks, three tracks for Amtrak's Northeast Corridor and MBTA commuter lines, and a 52-acre linear park.

name: Pruitt–Igoe, St. Louis
description: The Pruitt–Igoe public housing complex in St. Louis was built between 1951 and 1955. The first tenants moved into Pruitt in November 1954 and into Igoe in July 1955.
failedFuture: Modern public housing as the answer to the slum. The first building was demolished by explosives on 16 March 1972 and the site was fully cleared by 1976. Charles Jencks called the demolition 'the day Modern architecture died' (The Language of Post-Modern Architecture, 1984, p. 9).
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Verificada con Wikipedia. Katharine Bristol (1991) y Eugene Meehan (1979) discuten las causas; la ficha no atribuye una causa única.

presentEffect.text: A significant part of the site remains vacant as of 2023. An elementary school (1995), a planned medical facility (2020) and an urgent care centre (2022) have been built or planned there. The case became a symbol of modernism's failures and a case study for Oscar Newman's defensible space theory.

name: EPCOT, Walt Disney's city of tomorrow
description: Walt Disney's film for the Experimental Prototype Community of Tomorrow was shot on 27 October 1966, two months before his death. It imagined a city of about 20,000 citizens, most of them living in high-density apartments.
failedFuture: A working city of the future. What opened in 1982 was EPCOT Center, a theme park closer to a world's fair than a city.
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Verificada con Wikipedia; la afirmación sobre Celebration tiene una fuente débil y debe mejorarse.

presentEffect.text: EPCOT Center opened in 1982 as a theme park. Wikipedia says the concept influenced the nearby community of Celebration, Florida, but cites a Brazilian travel website (orlandoviagem.com.br, 2012) for that claim, a weak source.

name: Eliel Saarinen's Tribune Tower entry, 1922
description: Eliel Saarinen's entry to the 1922 Chicago Tribune Tower competition placed second. The competition received more than 260 entries, and the neo-Gothic design of John Mead Howells and Raymond Hood won.
failedFuture: A skyscraper design that came second and was not built, while the winning neo-Gothic tower rose beside the Chicago River.
license: Derechos vigentes de los autores (Gropius d. 1969, Meyer d. 1929). Verificar la imagen.
status: Sustituye la ficha de Gropius y Meyer, cuyo efecto presente no está documentado. Efecto presente verificado en Wikipedia, sin autor nombrado para la afirmación de influencia.

presentEffect.text: Wikipedia says Saarinen's entry was a strong influence on the next generation of skyscrapers, including Raymond Hood's McGraw-Hill Building and Rockefeller Center. The 1929 Gulf Building in Houston is described as a close realisation of it, and César Pelli's 181 West Madison Street building in Chicago is thought to be inspired by it.
presentEffect.source: Wikipedia, "Tribune Tower" (no author named for the influence claim).

name: Cumbernauld Town Centre, 1967
description: The Centre Cumbernauld was opened on 25 May 1967 by Princess Margaret and Lord Snowdon.
failedFuture: A megastructure town centre. It was twice named Scotland's worst town centre by the Carbuncle Awards, and in 2001 the judging panel called it 'a rabbit warren on stilts'.
source: Wikipedia, "The Centre Cumbernauld" (citing David Leask, HeraldScotland, 10 March 2022; Historic Environment Scotland, 23 November 2022).
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Verificada con Wikipedia. Año de concepción no confirmado; se usa 1967 como año de apertura.

presentEffect.text: North Lanarkshire Council announced plans to demolish it in March 2022. Historic Environment Scotland decided not to list it on 23 November 2022, citing advanced redevelopment plans, and the council bought the centre in June 2023.

name: Robin Hood Gardens, London
description: The Robin Hood Gardens housing estate in east London, by Alison and Peter Smithson, was built from 1968 and completed in 1972; the first flats opened in 1971.
failedFuture: A housing estate that was taken down in two phases. Tower Hamlets Council passed the demolition plans on 15 March 2012, the western block was demolished in 2017–2018, and the eastern block between mid-2024 and March 2025.
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Verificada con Wikipedia. El cierre (1972) es el de la finalización; la demolición va de 2017 a 2025.

presentEffect.text: The Victoria and Albert Museum salvaged a three-storey section of the estate, which was presented at the 2018 Venice Architecture Biennale.

name: The London Ringways
description: The London Ringways plan was part of the Greater London Development Plan published in 1969, and proposed a network of motorway rings around the city.
failedFuture: A set of urban motorways for London. The plan 'almost immediately attracted opposition from several directions', and the cabinet cancelled funding in 1973 after Labour's strong showing in the April 1973 GLC elections.
source: Wikipedia, "London Ringways" (citing Wayne Asher, Rings Around London, 2018).
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Verificada con Wikipedia; fuente principal citada: Wayne Asher (2018), no consultada.

presentEffect.text: Parts of the M25 were built from sections of Ringways 3 and 4. The A406 North Circular remained a trunk road, and the Westway (1970) and a section of the West Cross Route (1970) between North Kensington and Shepherd's Bush still exist.

name: Hulme Crescents, Manchester
description: The Hulme Crescents in Manchester were built around 1972 as part of a redevelopment already underway in 1969.
failedFuture: Crescent-shaped blocks of flats meant to rehouse a neighbourhood. Damp, pests and asbestos made the flats unfit to live in; in 1991 the government gave Manchester £31 million and a 'tabula rasa approach' was decided, with demolition from 1993 to 1995.
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Verificada con Wikipedia. La demolición es de 1993 a 1995 (no 1993–1994).

presentEffect.text: Hulme was redeveloped in the 1990s with low- to medium-rise housing. Homes for Change, a housing co-operative formed by some former residents, built a block that copies the estate's medium-rise form and 'the decks'.

name: Arcosanti, 1970
description: Paolo Soleri began building Arcosanti in 1970. The goal was for it to house 5,000 people.
failedFuture: A dense town for 5,000. The population has tended to vary between 50 and 150 people, many of them students and volunteers; thirteen major structures were built, the most recent finished in 1989.
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Verificada con Wikipedia, que avisa de referencias desactualizadas; pendiente contrastar con una fuente oficial.

presentEffect.text: Arcosanti still stands and is occupied by a small community, and construction has continued at a varying pace.
presentEffect.source: Wikipedia, "Arcosanti" (parts of the article rely on outdated references).

name: Futuro house
description: Fewer than 100 Futuro houses were made; a 2015 estimate counted around 60 survivors.
failedFuture: A plastic house for the future. The 1973 oil crisis led to an abrupt halt in plastic production and made synthetics very expensive, and public reception and ecological concern about plastics also weighed.
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Verificada con Wikipedia. Año de diseño no confirmado (la fuente solo menciona 1968 para una unidad en Tampa); se usa 1973 como año de la parada.

presentEffect.text: Around 60 Futuro houses were estimated to survive in 2015 (The Guardian, Jill Papworth).

name: Ville Radieuse
description: Le Corbusier's Radiant City, a 1930 plan for a city of towers in parkland, with housing blocks on pilotis, offices and elevated highways.
failedFuture: A city of towers in parkland with housing blocks on pilotis, offices and elevated highways, presented by Le Corbusier in 1930. It was never built as a whole city.
source: Museum of Modern Art (MoMA), "Le Corbusier" (collection, work 961).
license: Obras de Le Corbusier: derechos vigentes (FLC). Pedir autorización o usar la ficha del MoMA.
status: Hecho verificado en la Fondation Le Corbusier (inauguración 14 de octubre de 1952; sigue habitada). El nexo con la Ville Radieuse es interpretación y está marcado como tal.

presentEffect.text: The Unité d'Habitation in Marseille, known as the Cité Radieuse, was inaugurated on 14 October 1952 and is still inhabited. That this building carries the idea of the Radiant City is an interpretation drawn from its name: the Fondation Le Corbusier page names it 'Cité Radieuse' and mentions a 'vertical garden city' idea, but does not cite the Ville Radieuse.
presentEffect.source: Fondation Le Corbusier, "The Unité d'Habitation de Marseille turns 70".

name: Ordos Kangbashi, 2003
description: In 2003 Ordos city officials launched the creation of a new district for one million people; official construction began in 2004.
failedFuture: A city of one million. In 2014 the vacancy rate for new homes was reported at 70% (Woodworth, 2015).
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Verificada con Wikipedia; las cifras difieren entre fuentes y se muestran como tales.

presentEffect.text: Almost 120,000 people lived there in 2021 (Australian Financial Review); the 2020 district figure is 118,796. Wade Shepard reported about 153,000 in 2017 (Forbes).
presentEffect.source: Wikipedia, "Kangbashi District" (citing Australian Financial Review, 2021; Forbes, 2017).

name: Songdo International Business District
description: Construction of Songdo International Business District in South Korea started in 2003.
failedFuture: A city planned for 80,000 apartments by 2015. The expected completion date is now 2030.
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Verificada con Wikipedia; la fuente da dos fechas de finalización (2015 original y 2030 actual).

presentEffect.text: About 167,000 people lived there in June 2020, according to the Incheon Free Economic Zone Authority.
presentEffect.source: Wikipedia, "Songdo International Business District" (citing IFEZ population statistics, June 2020).

name: Germania
description: Albert Speer's plan for Germania, the planned capital of a Nazi empire: an east–west axis, a Great Hall about 200 metres high, and a triumphal arch of almost 100 metres. Demolition began in 1938.
failedFuture: A new capital for a thousand-year empire, planned around monumental axes through Berlin. Construction was halted in March 1943 and almost nothing of it was built.
license: Obras de Speer (murió en 1981): derechos vigentes. Verificar la licencia de cada imagen.
status: Efecto presente verificado en Brettin (Berliner Zeitung, 2020). Fechas 1938, 1943 del registro anterior.

presentEffect.text: About 800 of Speer's two-armed candelabra street lamps from 1939 still stand between Theodor-Heuss-Platz and S-Bahnhof Tiergarten, and the Schwerbelastungskörper (1941), a load-bearing test structure built to test Berlin's soil, still stands in Tempelhof.
presentEffect.source: Michael Brettin, Berliner Zeitung, 10 December 2020, "Germania: what's left of Hitler's fantasy capital".

name: Jeddah Tower
description: Construction of Jeddah Tower began on 1 April 2013. It was planned to be the first 1-kilometre-tall building.
failedFuture: A tower of 1,000 metres. In January 2018 the owner stopped structural concrete work because of labour issues with a contractor; work briefly resumed in 2018 and stalled again in 2020 due to COVID-19.
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Verificada con Wikipedia. Caso abierto: el proyecto no está cancelado, está en obras.

presentEffect.text: Work resumed in 2023 after a request for proposals, and construction officially restarted in January 2025.

name: Dubai Creek Tower
description: Groundbreaking for Dubai Creek Tower took place in October 2016. Emaar had originally discussed a minimum height of at least 1,300 metres.
failedFuture: A tower taller than the Burj Khalifa. Construction was halted on 4 April 2020 because of COVID-19 and delayed indefinitely as of 7 December 2020.
source: Wikipedia, "Dubai Creek Tower" (citing Reuters, April 2020; Bloomberg, December 2020).
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Verificada con Wikipedia. Caso abierto: el proyecto no está cancelado.

presentEffect.text: Construction restarted in March 2024, and in February 2024 the height was reportedly reduced to less than that of the Burj Khalifa. In June 2026 Alabbar said the tender had been delayed.

name: Ciudad Lineal, Madrid
description: Arturo Soria (Madrid 1844–1920) first presented the linear city in the newspaper El Progreso in 1882. He founded the Compañía Madrileña de Urbanización in 1894, and the first section, 5.2 km long and 40 m wide between the Aragon road and Pinar de Chamartín, was finished in 1911.
failedFuture: 'The city of the future' (la ciudad del porvenir), with all the advances and comforts of its time. Of the original buildings only some single-family houses survived.
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Efecto verificado en el folleto del Ayuntamiento de Madrid. Cierre no confirmado: el tranvía línea 70 cerró en 1972 (Wikipedia), pero no se toma como cierre del proyecto.

presentEffect.text: Madrid City Council's heritage leaflet states that Soria's legacy is still perceived today in Calle de Arturo Soria, with low-rise housing and large tree-lined spaces; it lists the former offices and depots of the Compañía Madrileña de Urbanización (no. 12) and surviving villas such as Villa Sotera and Villa Luisiana, and marked the centenary of his death in 2020. Ciudad Lineal is one of Madrid's 21 districts.
presentEffect.source: Ayuntamiento de Madrid, itinerary leaflet "Ciudad Lineal"; Wikipedia, "Ciudad Lineal".

name: Broadacre City, 1932
description: Frank Lloyd Wright presented Broadacre City in The Disappearing City in 1932. Taliesin student interns built a 12-by-12-foot model of a hypothetical four-square-mile community, financed by Edgar Kaufmann and first displayed on 15 April 1935 at Rockefeller Center in New York.
failedFuture: A decentralised community that Wright kept refining in books and articles until his death in 1959. The page does not say why it was never built.
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Efecto presente verificado en Wikipedia. La ficha no da la fecha del ingreso del modelo al MoMA ni el motivo de que no se construyera.

presentEffect.text: The model is now at the Museum of Modern Art. The page describes Broadacre City as the 'apotheosis' of suburbia and says edge cities are an unplanned, incomplete version of it; Jane Jacobs's The Death and Life of Great American Cities (1961) criticised this kind of planning.

name: New Babylon
description: Constant Nieuwenhuys's New Babylon, 1959–1974: a utopian city of linked sectors raised above ground, where residents, 'homo ludens', move between games and leisure without work.
failedFuture: A city without work, made of linked sectors raised above the ground, where people would live as nomads and play would organise the day. Constant worked on it until 1974 and said it was 'safely stored away in a museum, waiting for more favorable times'.
license: Obras de Constant (murió en 2005): derechos vigentes. Verificar en la Stichting Constant.
status: Efecto presente atribuido a Laura Stamps y a Frans van Hilten (2016). El origen de las ideas se sitúa en 1956 según Atlas Obscura; se mantiene 1959 como inicio del proyecto.

presentEffect.text: Laura Stamps, curator of the Gemeentemuseum Den Haag exhibition, says Constant's concept of nomadism 'has, in a way, become a reality for a number of groups of people', such as freelancers and refugees, and compares his interconnected sectors to today's digital networks. Frans van Hilten (2016) writes 'wij leven allemaal in New Babylon' and notes a residential and shopping complex named New Babylon next to The Hague's Centraal station.
presentEffect.source: Atlas Obscura, "New Babylon, future cities, Constant Nieuwenhuys" (Laura Stamps quoted); Frans van Hilten, Cultureel Persbureau, 2016.

name: The Congress Hall, Nuremberg
description: The foundation stone of the Kongresshalle at the Nazi Party rally grounds was laid in 1935. The Nuremberg architects Ludwig and Franz Ruff designed it to provide 50,000 seats.
failedFuture: A congress hall for Nazi party rallies that 'remained unfinished and without a roof'.
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Efecto presente verificado en Wikipedia. La ficha no da el año en que se detuvo la obra.

presentEffect.text: The Documentation Center of the Nazi Party Rally Grounds has occupied the northern wing since 2001, and the Nuremberg Symphony Orchestra is based in the southern building, the Serenadenhof. In 2019 an 85 million euro plan to conserve the Zeppelinfeld stadium was announced, with completion targeted for 2025.

name: Masdar City, 2006
description: Masdar City, announced in 2006 in Abu Dhabi as a state-funded project with a reported budget of $22 billion. Its first six buildings were completed and occupied in October 2010.
failedFuture: A planned city with a personal rapid transit system. In October 2010 the transit system was not to expand beyond its pilot, completion slipped from 2020–2025 to an estimated 2030, and by 2023 the community covered less than a sixth of its intended area.
license: Obra de Tange (murió en 2005): derechos vigentes. Pedir autorización.
status: Sustituye Tokyo Bay Plan (sin efecto presente documentado). Verificada con Wikipedia; pendiente abrir AP 2023 o NYT 2023.

presentEffect.text: By 2023 about 15,000 people lived and worked there, including 5,000 residents. It is the headquarters of the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA), and hosts Siemens' regional headquarters and Khalifa University, among others.
presentEffect.source: Wikipedia, "Masdar City" (citing Associated Press, 2023; New York Times, 2023; Bloomberg Businessweek, 2011; The Guardian, 2016).

name: Prora, the Strength Through Joy resort
description: Construction of the Prora resort on Rügen began in 1936 under the Strength Through Joy programme; it was designed by Clemens Klotz to house 20,000 holidaymakers and stopped in 1939 with the war.
failedFuture: A seaside resort that Hitler wanted to be 'the most mighty and large one to ever have existed'. It was never completed and never used as a holiday resort.
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Efecto presente verificado en Wikipedia. La ficha no describe el estado de Prora en 2020; su última actualización detallada es de 2017.

presentEffect.text: The Documentation Centre Prora opened in 2000, and in 2011 a 402-bed youth hostel opened, the largest in Germany. From 2013 units were sold as summer homes, and in 2016 the first new apartments opened in Block 1 and the Prora Solitaire hotel opened in Block 2.

name: Lower Manhattan Expressway
description: Robert Moses first conceived the expressway in 1941 and submitted the plans in November 1959. The 1960 plan would have evicted about 2,000 families in 416 buildings and displaced 804 businesses.
failedFuture: An expressway across lower Manhattan carrying I-78. Jane Jacobs led the opposition; in July 1969 Mayor Lindsay dropped the plans, calling it 'dead for all time', and the Board of Estimate removed it from city maps in August 1969.
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Efecto presente verificado en Wikipedia. La ficha no dice que SoHo o Chinatown se hayan conservado por esto.

presentEffect.text: A 156-foot section under Chrystie Street was built, completed by January 1964, and never used because the expressway was cancelled. The Holland Tunnel remains I-78's only section in New York.

name: The Illinois, Frank Lloyd Wright's mile-high tower
description: Frank Lloyd Wright described The Illinois in his 1957 book A Testament: originally 528 stories, later revised to 365, with 18,460,000 square feet of gross area and parking for 15,000 cars and 100 helicopters.
failedFuture: A mile-high skyscraper. The page gives no definitive reason it was not built, and notes engineering concerns about wind sway and evacuation by 76 elevators.
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Efecto presente verificado en Wikipedia. La ficha fecha el diseño en 1957, no en 1956.

presentEffect.text: The page says Adrian Smith's Burj Khalifa and Jeddah Tower are said to have been inspired by The Illinois, and records Witold Rybczynski's 2010 Slate article on the Burj Khalifa and Wright's influence. A song titled The Illinois was released by Fang Island in 2010.

name: Aircraft Carrier City in Landscape
description: Hans Hollein's Aircraft Carrier City in Landscape (1964): a city shaped like a carrier, laid flat over a landscape, shown in drawings and photomontages.
failedFuture: A city that is a ship on land, with the flight deck as a public square. It was never built; the project remains a classic image of the 1960s megastructure.
source: Museum of Modern Art (MoMA), "Hans Hollein. Aircraft Carrier City in Landscape, project" (work 636).

name: A Plan for Tokyo, 1960
description: Kenzo Tange's 'A Plan for Tokyo, 1960' was presented at the World Design Congress in Tokyo. It proposed a megastructure spanning Tokyo Bay, about 18 km from downtown Tokyo to Chiba in its first stage, with three levels of traffic carrying up to 2.5 million people along a linear civic axis.
failedFuture: A city that would grow along a linear axis over the bay. The page says it 'was never implemented'; Peter Smithson denied its feasibility, and Christopher Alexander (1965) called it a 'beautiful' tree city.
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Efecto presente verificado en Wikipedia. La ficha no menciona exposiciones del plan.

presentEffect.text: The page says the plan introduced ideas into urban-planning discourse and initiated a 'megastructure movement'. It informed Tange's later work, including the Yamanashi Press and Broadcasting Centre and the Skopje plan, and the Metabolist modular vision influenced Archigram.

name: Fun Palace, Cedric Price
description: Cedric Price conceived the Fun Palace in 1961 in East London, developing it with the theatre director Joan Littlewood and the cybernetician Gordon Pask.
failedFuture: A flexible, changing space for leisure and learning. The page says it was 'never built'.
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Efecto presente verificado en Wikipedia. La ficha no da el año de abandono ni menciona la campaña Fun Palaces.

presentEffect.text: Its flexible space influenced Richard Rogers and Renzo Piano, whose Centre Georges Pompidou in Paris extended many of Price's ideas. Price used some of them on a smaller scale at the Inter-Action Centre in Kentish Town, London (1971), and the Canadian Centre for Architecture holds his archive.

name: Continuous Monument
description: Superstudio's Continuous Monument (1969): a photomontage of a monumental grid laid across the planet, where one continuous monolith covers the world.
failedFuture: An anti-architectural proposal: a single continuous monument covering the world, presented by Superstudio in 1969 as conceptual architecture. It was never built.
source: Museum of Modern Art (MoMA), "Superstudio, Continuous Monument" (work 938).
license: Obras de Superstudio: derechos vigentes. Pedir autorización o usar la ficha del MoMA.
status: Efecto presente atribuido a Jonathan Ringen vía Wikipedia; pendiente abrir su texto y concretar en qué obras se nota la influencia.

presentEffect.text: Critics regard Superstudio's work as influential on architects including Zaha Hadid, Rem Koolhaas and Bernard Tschumi (Jonathan Ringen, 'Superstudio Pioneers of Conceptual Architecture').
presentEffect.source: Wikipedia, "Superstudio" (citing Jonathan Ringen, 'Superstudio Pioneers of Conceptual Architecture').

name: Exodus, or the Voluntary Prisoners of Architecture
description: Rem Koolhaas, Elia and Zoe Zenghelis and Madelon Vriesendorp's Exodus (1972): a city of walled zones in which people live as 'voluntary prisoners' of architecture, shown in drawings and text.
failedFuture: A utopian and dystopian linear city cutting through London 'like a knife', in which people would live as voluntary prisoners of architecture. It was never built.
source: Museum of Modern Art (MoMA), "Exodus" (work 104692). JSTOR Daily, "Rem Koolhaas and the voluntary prisoners of architecture".
license: Obras de OMA y Zenghelis/Vriesendorp: derechos vigentes. Pedir autorización.
status: Hecho verificado en Wikipedia (OMA fundada en 1975 por los mismos autores). El nexo causal con la obra de OMA es interpretación.

presentEffect.text: Exodus was the first major joint project of Rem Koolhaas and Elia Zenghelis. The Office for Metropolitan Architecture (OMA) was founded in 1975 by the same authors, with Madelon Vriesendorp and Zoe Zenghelis. That Exodus led to OMA's later work is an interpretation: the source does not state it.

name: Cardiff Bay Opera House
description: Zaha Hadid's design for the Cardiff Bay Opera House, which won an international competition held in the 1990s, intended as a permanent home for the Welsh National Opera.
failedFuture: A Welsh opera house meant to crown the Cardiff Bay redevelopment. The Millennium Commission rejected the lottery bid on 22 December 1995, judging the project financially risky, and the project then collapsed.
license: Obra de Hadid (murió en 2016): derechos vigentes de Zaha Hadid Architects. Pedir autorización.
status: Corregido: el diseño es de Zaha Hadid (no de Jørn Utzon). Pendiente: año de concepción (la fuente solo dice 'años noventa'), por lo que la distancia no se calcula.

presentEffect.text: The Wales Millennium Centre opened on the intended site, with Phase 1 opening on 26–28 November 2004. It offered a broader range of arts while keeping an opera element.
presentEffect.source: Wikipedia, "Cardiff Bay Opera House" and "Wales Millennium Centre".
